title.en: Equilibrium, excess demand and excess supply

body.en: A market is in equilibrium when market demand equals market supply: $q^D(p^*) = q^S(p^*)$. The price $p^*$ is the equilibrium price and the quantity is the equilibrium quantity. If price is below $p^*$, quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied: excess demand. If price is above $p^*$, there is excess supply. In perfect competition, buyers and sellers are price takers, so we assume the market itself (Adam Smith's invisible hand) moves price toward equilibrium.

points.en: p < p*: excess demand → price rises
p > p*: excess supply → price falls

narration.en: Equilibrium is where market demand equals market supply. Below the equilibrium price there is excess demand; above it, excess supply.
narration.kn: ಮಾರುಕಟ್ಟೆ ಬೇಡಿಕೆ ಮಾರುಕಟ್ಟೆ ಪೂರೈಕೆಗೆ ಸಮವಾದಾಗ ಸಮತೋಲನ. ಸಮತೋಲನ ಬೆಲೆಗಿಂತ ಕೆಳಗೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚುವರಿ ಬೇಡಿಕೆ; ಮೇಲೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚುವರಿ ಪೂರೈಕೆ.

say.en: Demand is 300 minus 10p and supply is 50 plus 15p. Set them equal.
On the graph, the demand and supply curves cross at a price of 10 and quantity of 200.
At a price of 8, buyers want 220 but sellers offer only 170: excess demand of 50 pushes the price up.
At a price of 12, sellers offer 230 but buyers want only 180: excess supply of 50 pushes the price down.

narration.en: Demand is 300 minus 10p and supply is 50 plus 15p. Set them equal.

body.en: When there is excess demand, some buyers who cannot get the good are willing to pay more, so price rises; as it rises, quantity demanded falls and quantity supplied rises until the gap closes. When there is excess supply, sellers who cannot sell cut their prices; quantity demanded rises and quantity supplied falls until the gap closes. In this chapter we first take the number of firms as fixed.

points.en: Number of firms fixed in the short-run analysis

narration.en: Excess demand pushes price up and excess supply pushes it down, until demand and supply are equal again.

problem.en: Market demand is qD = 300 − 10p and market supply is qS = 50 + 15p. Find the equilibrium price and quantity, and the excess demand or supply at p = ₹8 and p = ₹12.

steps.en: At p = 8: qD = 220, qS = 170 → excess demand = 50.
At p = 12: qD = 180, qS = 230 → excess supply = 50.

answer.en: p* = ₹10, q* = 200; excess demand 50 at ₹8; excess supply 50 at ₹12.
